name: Starlink Terminal

placement_rationale.text: This entry represents the terminal's front-line use specifically, per its own text — a dugout or forward vehicle relaying drone video, not the rear-headquarters use of the same technology. A shallow tactical siting near doctrine.md §2's forward-CP depth (2-5km) fits that framing: the terminal is used at every echelon, but the 3km position captures the forward end deliberately singled out here.

cost.display: ~$385–700 per terminal; ~$50–100/month subscription (over 150,000 terminals reportedly in use across Ukraine, front and rear)

key_facts.label: Latency
key_facts.value: Low-earth-orbit — tens of milliseconds, usable for real-time video/control

key_facts.label: Deployment
key_facts.value: Man-portable, no fixed ground infrastructure needed

short_role: Low-earth-orbit satellite internet terminal that gives front-line units resilient connectivity independent of local infrastructure.
characteristics: Low latency relative to older geostationary satellite links — usable for real-time video and even some drone control links
No cell towers or fiber needed — works from a dugout, a vehicle, or a headquarters equally
Deployed at every echelon, not just the rear — this entry represents its front-line use specifically
employment_notes: Used everywhere from frontline positions relaying drone video to rear headquarters running battle-management software — a single commercial technology now underpins a large share of both tactical and operational communications, which concentrates real operational risk in one vendor's service decisions and ground-station footprint.
contrast_vs_traditional: Military communications used to mean purpose-built, hardened, service-specific radio and satellite networks built to survive jamming and destruction. A big share of this war's comms backbone is instead a commercial internet service never designed as a weapon system — which is exactly why EW is described as the invisible battlefield everything else depends on: lose reliable comms and the fast kill chains built on top of it, from drone feeds to fire missions, collapse back toward the old multi-hour model.
